Question: AI factory network (ai data center design)
Answer: the set of separate fabrics (compute, converged north-south, out-of-band management) that connect GPU servers, storage and users in an AI data center.

Question: Compute fabric (ai data center design)
Answer: the east-west RDMA network that carries GPU-to-GPU traffic during training.

Question: Scalable unit (SU) (ai data center design)
Answer: a repeatable building block of servers and network ports; clusters scale by replicating SUs.

Question: SuperNIC (ai data center design)
Answer: an NVIDIA network adapter (such as BlueField-3 SuperNIC or ConnectX-8) used on the Spectrum-X compute fabric for lossless RoCE.

Question: BlueField-3 DPU (ai data center design)
Answer: a data processing unit that connects a node to the converged north-south network in the enterprise reference architecture.

Question: Rail-optimized topology (ai data center design)
Answer: a wiring pattern where the GPUs with the same index in each server connect to the same leaf switches, so same-rail traffic stays within one switch hop.

Question: Spectrum-X Multiplane (ai data center design)
Answer: a Spectrum-X capability that splits each SuperNIC across independent network planes to improve resiliency and scale.

Question: RDMA (ai data center design)
Answer: remote direct memory access: a NIC moves data directly between the memory of two machines without involving their CPUs in each transfer.

Question: GPUDirect RDMA (ai data center design)
Answer: a path where the network adapter reads and writes GPU memory directly, avoiding a copy through host memory.

Question: RoCE (RDMA over Converged Ethernet) (spectrum networking)
Answer: RDMA carried over Ethernet, which depends on a lossless or near-lossless fabric.

Question: Lossless RoCE mode (spectrum networking)
Answer: the NVUE RoCE mode that enables PFC on the RoCE priority together with ECN; it is the default.

Question: Lossy RoCE mode (spectrum networking)
Answer: the NVUE RoCE mode that uses ECN without PFC.

Question: PFC (spectrum networking)
Answer: priority flow control: pauses one traffic class on a link when buffers fill so RoCE traffic is not dropped.

Question: ECN (spectrum networking)
Answer: explicit congestion notification: marks packets when a queue passes a threshold so senders slow down before loss occurs.

Question: EVPN (spectrum networking)
Answer: the standards-based BGP control plane for VXLAN that distributes MAC and IP reachability between VTEPs.

Question: L3 VNI (spectrum networking)
Answer: the VXLAN network identifier that maps a tenant VRF so routed traffic stays inside that tenant.

Question: VRF (spectrum networking)
Answer: a virtual routing and forwarding instance: a separate routing table per tenant.

Question: DSX Air (spectrum networking)
Answer: NVIDIA's cloud-based platform for simulating AI factory networks and software before hardware is installed.

Question: WJH (What Just Happened) (spectrum networking)
Answer: the switch service and agent that report why packets were dropped, grouped by layer and channel.

Question: Channel (WJH) (spectrum networking)
Answer: a named group of WJH drop triggers (forwarding, layer-1, buffer, ACL) with its own polling interval and cache size.

Question: NetQ (spectrum networking)
Answer: NVIDIA's fabric-wide monitoring platform that collects switch telemetry, events and WJH data, with a UI and CLI.

Question: DOCA (spectrum networking)
Answer: NVIDIA's SDK and driver framework for BlueField DPUs and ConnectX and SuperNIC adapters; doca-all is the full host installation profile.

Question: Subnet manager (SM) (infiniband networking)
Answer: the control-plane software that discovers an InfiniBand fabric, assigns LIDs, computes routes and applies partitions and QoS; it can run on a switch, a host (OpenSM) or in UFM.

Question: UFM HA (infiniband networking)
Answer: an active/standby pair of UFM servers kept in sync with heartbeat and DRBD so a standby can take over fabric management.

Question: LinkDownedCounter (infiniband networking)
Answer: a port error counter read with perfquery; a very high value points to a flapping or corrupted link.

Question: PKey (partition key) (infiniband networking)
Answer: a 16-bit value carried in every InfiniBand packet that defines which partition (isolation domain) the traffic belongs to.

Question: Full and limited membership (infiniband networking)
Answer: the two membership types of a partition member, shown by the top bit of the PKey; limited is assumed when membership is omitted in partitions.conf.

Question: partitions.conf (infiniband networking)
Answer: the OpenSM file that defines partitions, their PKeys and member port GUIDs.

Question: Fabric segmentation (infiniband networking)
Answer: UFM's feature for assigning ports to PKeys and setting per-partition QoS parameters.

Question: Service level (SL) and virtual lane (VL) (infiniband networking)
Answer: the QoS tag in an InfiniBand packet (SL) and the independent buffer queue on a link (VL); an SL-to-VL map decides which VL carries each class.

Question: Adaptive routing (InfiniBand) (infiniband networking)
Answer: switch-side output port selection by load, configured by the subnet manager using LAG, TREE or DF_PLUS grouping.

Question: SHIELD (infiniband networking)
Answer: InfiniBand fast link fault recovery: switches choose an alternative port when a link fails, without waiting for the SM.

Question: ARN (infiniband networking)
Answer: Adaptive Routing Notification: a congested switch tells neighbor switches to pick another output port.

Question: UFM (Unified Fabric Manager) (infiniband networking)
Answer: NVIDIA's platform for InfiniBand fabric management, telemetry, health checks, events and partitioning.

Question: UFM Telemetry (infiniband networking)
Answer: the UFM component that collects per-port counters (error rates, temperature, histograms, retransmissions) for monitoring and prediction.

Question: Network Operator (kubernetes integration)
Answer: the NVIDIA Kubernetes operator that deploys and manages networking drivers, RDMA device plugins and secondary networks for NVIDIA NICs.

Question: NicClusterPolicy (kubernetes integration)
Answer: the custom resource that tells the Network Operator which components to deploy (OFED driver, RDMA shared device plugin and others).

Question: RDMA shared device plugin (kubernetes integration)
Answer: a Kubernetes device plugin that exposes RDMA-capable devices to pods as a named, shareable resource.

Question: Node Feature Discovery (NFD) (kubernetes integration)
Answer: a Kubernetes add-on that labels nodes with hardware features; the Network Operator requires it and deploys it by default.

Question: cl-resource-query (troubleshooting tools)
Answer: the Cumulus Linux tool that shows how much of the switch ASIC's forwarding and ACL resources are in use.

Question: Forwarding table profile (troubleshooting tools)
Answer: the setting that divides the ASIC's memory between MAC, neighbor and route entries.

Question: ibstat (troubleshooting tools)
Answer: lists each InfiniBand or RDMA adapter and port with state, physical state, link layer and rate.

Question: ib_write_bw (troubleshooting tools)
Answer: the perftest tool that measures RDMA write bandwidth between a server and a client.

Question: ib_write_lat (troubleshooting tools)
Answer: the perftest tool that measures RDMA write latency between a server and a client.

Question: ibnodes (troubleshooting tools)
Answer: lists the InfiniBand nodes (channel adapters and switches) in the subnet topology.

Question: iblinkinfo (troubleshooting tools)
Answer: reports link information for each port in the fabric, node by node.

Question: ibping (troubleshooting tools)
Answer: validates connectivity between InfiniBand nodes using vendor management datagrams, in client/server mode.

Question: ibdiagnet (troubleshooting tools)
Answer: the NVIDIA InfiniBand fabric diagnostic tool.

Question: The startup file (automation and configuration)
Answer: "NVUE saves the configuration in a configuration file called /etc/nvue.d/startup.yaml."

Question: NVUE (automation and configuration)
Answer: NVIDIA User Experience: the Cumulus Linux configuration system, with a CLI, a REST API and a startup.yaml file.

Question: startup.yaml (automation and configuration)
Answer: the file /etc/nvue.d/startup.yaml where NVUE saves the configuration applied at boot.

Question: NVUE snippet (automation and configuration)
Answer: raw YAML applied with nv config patch for features NVUE does not yet expose; it is not validated by NVUE.

Question: nvidia.nvue (automation and configuration)
Answer: NVIDIA's Ansible collection for devices managed by NVUE, with CLI, REST API and object-specific modules.

Question: Production Ready Automation (PRA) (automation and configuration)
Answer: NVIDIA's reference topology with playbooks and the jinja2 template that renders startup.yaml.
